QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_4

question.text: Nilgiri Multi-Strategy Fund (open-ended Cat III) had a pre-side-pocket NAV of INR 100 per unit. An illiquid position representing 12% of gross assets is segregated into a side-pocket. What are the NAVs of the main and side-pocket units immediately post-segregation, assuming pari-passu allocation?

explanation.text: The Logic: On side-pocket creation, the unit's pre-event NAV of 100 is split pro-rata to the liquid vs illiquid bucket value. 12% illiquid -> side-pocket NAV = 12; 88% liquid -> main NAV = 88. Together they sum back to the original 100. Each original unit-holder receives one main unit + one side-pocket unit; new subscribers after the event invest only in the main series. The Trap: Option A zeroes the side-pocket (wrong — value is segregated, not written off). Option C puts 100 on the side-pocket (double counting). Option D inflates the main NAV (net increase is impossible without PnL). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) frames side-pockets as a client-communication issue. XIX-E tests the segregation math. Mutual funds also permit side-pockets under credit-event triggers — XV (RA) / X-A (IA L1) reference. Manager's Pro-Tip: On side-pocket day, freeze subscriptions and redemptions in the main scheme for a cut-off; run parallel NAV for main and side-pocket; accrue no management fee on the side-pocket until realisation. Crystallise HWM on the side-pocket separately — most Cat III PPMs stop performance fee on frozen side-pocket units.
